title: An edge-bicolored graph approach to the Ising model on random regular graphs
authors: Michael Borinsky, Shiyue Ren, Maximilian Wiesmann
abstract: We give an exact solution of the ferromagnetic Ising model on a random regular graph ensemble via analytic combinatorics. Expressing the partition function as the generating function of labeled edge-bicolored graphs, we obtain the free energy in the thermodynamic limit from the asymptotic enumeration of these graphs. A simple analysis of the resulting formula reveals a second-order phase transition with critical exponents of the mean-field universality class.
summary: This paper provides an exact solution for the free energy of the Ising model on random regular graphs using advanced analytic combinatorics. It rigorously proves that the system undergoes a second-order phase transition at a specific critical temperature, confirming mean-field critical exponents. The methodology involves mapping the partition function to counting weighted edge-bicolored graphs in the thermodynamic limit.
main_problem: The primary goal is to find an exact solution for the free energy of the ferromagnetic Ising model defined on a random regular graph ensemble.
main_result: The model exhibits a second-order phase transition at a critical temperature $T_c$, and the critical exponents ($\alpha=0,  eta_{mag}=1/2, \gamma=1, \delta=3$) match those of the mean-field universality class.
method: The authors use analytic combinatorics by expressing the partition function as a generating function for labeled edge-bicolored graphs and calculating its asymptotic enumeration in the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The system is the Ising model ($	ext{Z}_2$ spin system) defined on a random $k$-regular graph ensemble. The Hamiltonian includes ferromagnetic coupling ($J>0$) and an external magnetic field ($h$).
key_observables: Free energy in the thermodynamic limit, spontaneous magnetization $m_0( eta)$, and critical exponents ($\alpha,  eta_{mag}, \gamma, \delta$).

main_assumptions: The calculation yields an *annealed* free energy, and the analysis relies on identifying a unique global maximum of auxiliary functions derived from asymptotic enumeration.

paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the partition function and using high-temperature expansions to deriving an identity involving subgraphs. It then uses asymptotic enumeration techniques (saddle point approximation) on these graph counts to determine the free energy in the thermodynamic limit, culminating in the calculation of critical exponents.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical tools developed—analytic combinatorics applied to large random structures—are highly relevant for analyzing complex quantum many-body systems where exact enumeration is intractable.
